draft.title: Projectile motion
card: A projectile is any object or body moving through the air with only gravity and air resistance acting on it. Examples are a thrown javelin or a long jumper in flight.
Three factors set the flight: release speed, release angle and release height. They are fixed at the moment of release or take-off.
A greater release speed gives a longer flight distance. A greater release height also adds distance, because the object has further to fall before it lands.
A release angle near 45° gives the greatest distance when release and landing heights are equal. A steeper angle gives more height but less distance, and a lower angle gives less of both.
draft.remember: Speed, angle and height at release decide the flight. Nothing the athlete does in the air changes the path much.

a.q: A shot putter keeps the same release speed and height but changes the release angle from 40° to 70°. What is the most likely result?
opts: The shot goes higher but travels a shorter distance
The shot goes higher and travels a greater distance
The shot goes lower and travels a shorter distance
The shot goes lower but travels a greater distance
a.why: A steeper angle sends more of the speed upwards, so the shot rises higher. Less is left for forward motion, so the distance falls. A steeper angle does not always give more distance, because 45° is near the best for equal heights.
a.clue: Steeper means more upward and less forward.

b.q: Two basketball players release shots at the same speed and angle. Ana shoots from a standing position and Ben shoots in a jump with a higher release point. Which statement about the flight is correct?
opts: Ben's shot can travel further, as it falls from higher
Ana's shot can travel further, as it is released lower
Both shots travel equally far, as speed and angle match
Ben's shot can travel less far, as it spends longer rising
b.why: Release height is one of the three factors. A higher release point means the ball has further to fall, so it stays in the air longer and can travel further. Matching speed and angle does not make the flights equal when the heights differ.
b.clue: Which of the three release factors is different here?

a.best: The shot goes higher but travels a shorter distance

b.best: Ben's shot can travel further, as it falls from higher
